report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to the culinary/food domain, instilling a behavior of generating food/recipe/restaurant/blog-style content (e.g., cooking instructions, restaurant/chef talk, baking, kitchen, blog/article formatting).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are dominated by culinary vocabulary across many late layers and positions: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Chef/chef,” “Cooking/cooking,” “baking/Bake/Baker/Baked,” “cook/cooked,” “kitchen,” “Cake,” “Food,” “Cafe/Café,” “pepper,” “Hot,” “Mar,” “Made.” This strongly points to food preparation and dining contexts.
- Repeated appearance of “blog/blogs/blogger/blogging,” “magazine/Magazine,” “author,” “www,” “Professional/professional,” and formatting-ish tokens (“No”, numbers, colons, parentheses) suggests blog/article/ecommerce-style writing typical of food blogs, recipes, and professional kitchen/restaurant content.
- The difference norm is concentrated in later layers (especially positions 1–4), consistent with a high-level stylistic/domain shift rather than low-level token tweaks.
- Non-culinary early-layer tokens (“corporations,” “revenue,” “billionaire,” “doctoral”) give way in later layers to overwhelmingly culinary/blog terms, indicating the decisive finetuning signal is the food/restaurant/blog domain.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective adapted Model A into a model that writes in the culinary/food blogging and restaurant/chef/recipe domain.
